title: Maps, Plans and Scale
summary: Number and bar scales, measuring real distances on maps and plans, using grid references and compass directions, reading floor plans, and following directions.

rows: 1 unit on the map = 50 000 of the same units in real life
Measure on the map and compare with the bar

notes.label: Why bar scales are useful
notes.text: If a map is enlarged or reduced on a photocopier, a **bar scale** stays correct because it changes size with the map, but a number scale does not.

notes.title: Worked example 1: real distance
notes.problem: On a map with scale 1 : 50 000, two towns are 7,4 cm apart. What is the real distance in km?

notes.title: Worked example 2: map distance
notes.problem: A road is 12 km long. How long is it on a map with scale 1 : 200 000?

notes.title: Worked example 3
notes.problem: A 3 m wall is drawn as 6 cm on a plan. Write the scale as a ratio.

items: **Grid references** (e.g. C4) locate places on street maps: letters for columns and numbers for rows.
**Compass directions**: N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, NW.
Directions use landmarks and turns: 'Turn left into Church Street, pass the clinic on your right, and take the second road on the left.'

notes.text: A **floor plan** shows the layout of a building from above, drawn to scale, with symbols for doors (an arc showing which way they open), windows (thin double lines in the wall), and fittings such as baths and stoves.

questions.prompt: On a 1 : 100 000 map, the route from home to a stadium is 18 cm. If a taxi travels at an average of 60 km/h, how long will the trip take?
questions.memo:
✓ Real distance = 18 km (1)
✓ Time = 18 ÷ 60 = 0,3 h (1)
✓ = 18 minutes (1)

questions.prompt: On a 1 : 100 plan, a lounge measures 5 cm by 4 cm. Carpet costs R245 per m². Calculate the cost of carpeting the lounge.
Give TWO things that make written directions easy to follow.
questions.memo: Any two (1 each): use landmarks; give turns clearly (left/right); give distances or number of streets; use street names; give compass directions
